claims.statement: A single scalar BPM is insufficient to represent the current project evidence: the original mix fallback estimate, drums-stem fallback estimate, Studio header and exported MIDI tempo map do not collapse to one identical value.

The preservation A and preferred working B artifacts are extremely close waveforms while B carries the operator preference label; renderer learning therefore needs controlled listening labels and should not infer preference from gross similarity alone.
The all-zero Contrast Audition artifact is invalid for semantic or preference calibration and must be excluded rather than treated as a negative musical example.

contradictions.a: Studio project header observed at 103 BPM
contradictions.b: Exported MIDI tempo events observed from 94.87666034155598 to 102.51153254741159 BPM with median 100.65425264217413 BPM
contradictions.reason: A project header scalar and an exported tempo-event map represent different surfaces; neither is silently rewritten into the other.
Different signals can produce different beat-tracker interpretations; Beat This must be run separately before any model calibration conclusion.
